title: Burden of proof: Bellarmine must prove Mass and Roman sacraments, not demand our disproof
source_text: XI. Iniquum est autem, & contra disputationis leges, quod Bellarminus a nobis exigit, nempe, ut ostendamus caetera illa quae Paulus dispositurum se promittit, non esse graviora quaedam de sacrificio, scilicet, altaris, & Sacramentorum Ecclesiae Romanae materia & forma. Cum enim hoc in loco Bellarminus argumentetur, nos vero respondeamus, Bellarmini est probare quae dicit, nobis vero sufficit propositiones illius negare, & nostras asserere. Itaque non debuit simpliciter dicere, sed demonstrare Paulum aliquid ordinasse de sacrificio Missae, & illis Ecclesiae Romanae Sacramentis, quae nos adulterina & notha judicamus.
pass_a_gloss: But it is unfair, and against the laws of disputation, that Bellarmine demands of us, namely, that we show that those remaining things which Paul promises he will arrange are not certain graver things concerning the sacrifice of the altar and the matter and form of the Sacraments of the Roman Church. For since Bellarmine is arguing in this place, and we are answering, it is Bellarmine's to prove what he says, but for us it is enough to deny his propositions and assert ours. Therefore he ought not simply to have said, but to have demonstrated that Paul ordered something concerning the sacrifice of the Mass, and those Sacraments of the Roman Church which we judge adulterous and spurious.
pass_b_english: He may not shift the burden: we need not disprove Mass and Roman sacrament forms.
He argues; we answer — he must prove his fill-ins.
Denial of his propositions is enough until he demonstrates them.
Show that Paul ordered Mass sacrifice and those sacraments we call spurious — or drop the claim.

choices.english: it is Bellarmine's to prove what he says
